summary: The Time off calendar gains a fourth window, Range, and stops refusing to draw anything when Teams or People is chosen with nothing ticked. Three things change together. (1) packages/validation loses TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES.teamsRequired and .peopleRequired — deleted, not deprecated, so every consumer stops compiling — and gains the range arithmetic the new window needs (step by the range's own length, Today keeping the length, and the anchor a range converts to). (2) apps/api/src/time-off/time-off-calendar.service.ts drops the two 422s and, critically, makes an empty projectIds / memberIds mean *no narrowing* rather than the empty id filter it would otherwise become — `id: { in: [] }` returns zero rows, which is the exact wrong answer this spec forbids. (3) The screen adds the Range segment, a DateRangePicker whose ends become startDate/endDate unchanged, prev/next/Today under a custom range, and a day-column floor with a horizontal scroll so a 92-column grid is readable. The design system's DateRangePicker gains one optional prop — a span bound applied once a start is armed — because REQ-03-009 cannot be expressed with the fixed minDate/maxDate it has today. No route is added, no response body changes shape, no entity, no column, no migration.

tasks.title: packages/validation — delete the two withdrawn messages, add the custom-range arithmetic
detail: Delete `teamsRequired` and `peopleRequired` from TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MESSAGES (packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts:27-28). REQ-03-003 and the Withdrawn table of the contracts file: deleted, never left unreferenced. The remaining five 422 messages and the four screen-only strings are unchanged, verbatim.

Remove the two assertions that pin the deleted text in packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.test.ts:137-138. Every other assertion in that `carries the tabulated message text, verbatim` case stays.

REQ-03-007 — the fourth window. Do NOT widen `TimeOffCalendarWindow` (currently 'week' | '2weeks' | 'month'): it is the parameter of `timeOffCalendarWindowRange` and `stepTimeOffCalendarAnchor`, both of which are anchor-driven and have no meaning for a span the reader picked by hand. Add `export type TimeOffCalendarWindowChoice = TimeOffCalendarWindow | 'range'` and let the screen hold that. State the reason in the doc comment.

REQ-03-011 — `export function stepTimeOffCalendarRange(range: TimeOffCalendarRange, direction: -1 | 1): TimeOffCalendarRange`. Both ends move by `calendarDaySpan(range.startDate, range.endDate)` days in `direction`; the span is preserved by construction (move both ends by the same number). TC-03-UNIT-11 checks a 10-day span both ways and a one-day span.

REQ-03-012 — `export function timeOffCalendarRangeToday(range: TimeOffCalendarRange, today: string): TimeOffCalendarRange`. Start becomes `today`; end becomes `addCalendarDays(today, span - 1)` where `span` is the input's span. TC-03-UNIT-12 checks a 10-day range not containing today, and a one-day range.

REQ-03-013 — `export function timeOffCalendarAnchorFromRange(range: TimeOffCalendarRange): string` returning `range.startDate`. It is one line and it exists so the rule 'a preset opens on the window containing the range's start' has one definition rather than being retyped in the screen. TC-03-UNIT-13 asserts `timeOffCalendarWindowRange('month', timeOffCalendarAnchorFromRange(range), 'Monday')` is the month containing a mid-month start.

REQ-03-017 — the reverse direction needs no new function: seeding Range from a preset is `timeOffCalendarWindowRange(preset, anchor, firstDayOfWeek)`, which already returns exactly `{ startDate, endDate }`. TC-03-UNIT-13's second half asserts that against a month window. Do not add a wrapper that only forwards.

REQ-03-009 — `export function timeOffCalendarLatestEnd(startDate: string): string` = `addCalendarDays(startDate, TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_RANGE_DAYS - 1)`, i.e. start + 91. The 92-day bound is inclusive (Validation Rule 3, Edge case 6), so the last permitted end is 91 days after the start. The screen and the picker both read this; neither restates the arithmetic.

`packages/validation` resolves through `dist/` (package.json main/types), which is gitignored and built by `npm run build --workspace @devscribed/validation`. Run that build after editing, or the API, the web app and the static gate's typecheck all keep seeing the deleted exports.

tasks.title: DateRangePicker — bound the span once a start is armed
detail: REQ-03-009 needs the panel to stop offering an end more than 91 days after the armed start. The component cannot express that today: `minDate` / `maxDate` are fixed props, and the armed start is the component's own `pending` state, which no consumer can see (DateRangePicker.tsx:87, :124-127).

Add one optional prop — `maxSpanDays?: number` — documented as the inclusive number of days the committed range may cover. While `pending` is null it changes nothing. While `pending` is set, `selectable` additionally excludes every date after `addDays(pending, maxSpanDays - 1)`; `Calendar` renders those days with a real `disabled` (its `availableDates` contract, Calendar.tsx:22-23), and the arrow walk skips them.

Apply the bound to `availableDates` **only**, never to the `minDate` / `maxDate` handed to `Calendar`: those two gate the month arrows (Calendar.tsx:175-176), and narrowing them would stop the reader paging to the month their end date is in.

The date arithmetic stays inside this file — `packages/ds` does not depend on `@devscribed/validation` and will not (the note at DateRangePicker.tsx:41-44). Add a small local day-shift on the ISO string through `Date.UTC`, matching how `monthWeeks` already reads a `CalendarDate` off the string.

The prop is optional and the three shipped consumers pass nothing, so their behaviour is unchanged: apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/reports/amounts-owed/page.tsx:440, .../reports/time-and-activity/page.tsx:511, .../reports/time-off/page.tsx:415.
No new export from packages/ds/src/index.ts is needed — `DateRangePickerProps` is already exported (index.ts:141) and gains the field.
No hardcoded colour or size: this task adds behaviour, not paint.

tasks.title: The calendar screen — the Range window, the picker, the nav under a custom range, and the grid's floor
detail: REQ-03-005 / REQ-03-016 — delete the two client-side short-circuits at CalendarScreen.tsx:198-212. REQ-03-007 — a fourth segment in WINDOW_SEGMENTS: `{ value: 'range', label: 'Range', testId: 'calendar-window-range' }`. `ToggleButton`'s `options` form already takes any number of segments and gives each its own test id and arrow-key stop. Range is a window, not a mode: all four stay in the one control.

State: hold the choice as `TimeOffCalendarWindowChoice` and keep a separate `customRange: TimeOffCalendarRange` beside the existing `anchor`. The window that is fetched is `timeOffCalendarWindowRange(preset, anchor, firstDayOfWeek)` under a preset and `customRange` under Range. The window, the scope and the range stay in-page state and out of the URL (Actors & Preconditions; time-off/01's decision, restated here).

REQ-03-008 — while Range is active, draw `<DateRangePicker>` in the filter row beside the pickers, `data-testid="calendar-range-picker"` on the component (it spreads the rest onto its root) and `triggerTestId="calendar-range-picker-trigger"`. `onChange` writes the two ends into `customRange` unchanged — no rounding to a week, no clamping. Both ids are absent while any preset is active.

REQ-03-009 — pass `maxSpanDays={TIME_OFF_CALENDAR_MAX_RANGE_DAYS}` (T4's prop). The panel then offers no end more than 91 days after the armed start, which is what `timeOffCalendarLatestEnd` computes and what TC-03-E2E-12 reads. The bound is forward-only, exactly as REQ-03-009 states; a reader who arms a start and clicks a much earlier day still commits a legal-or-refused range, and Edge case 7 is the answer when it is over 92 days.

REQ-03-011 — `calendar-prev` / `calendar-next` call `stepTimeOffCalendarRange(customRange, ∓1)` while Range is active, and keep calling `stepTimeOffCalendarAnchor` under the three presets. Both ends move by the range's own length; the length is preserved (Edge case 9).

REQ-03-012 — `calendar-today` sets `customRange = timeOffCalendarRangeToday(customRange, today())` while Range is active, and keeps setting the anchor under a preset. `today()` stays the account-timezone reading already in the file (CalendarScreen.tsx:136) — never the browser clock.
REQ-03-013 — leaving Range for a preset sets `anchor = timeOffCalendarAnchorFromRange(customRange)`; the preset then opens on the window containing that start (Edge case 11).
REQ-03-017 — entering Range from a preset seeds `customRange` with that preset's current `range` (Edge case 12: Month → Range is that month's first and last day).

The range label. `rangeLabel` takes the window and two dates; give it the Range case — the same `d Mon yyyy – d Mon yyyy` shape the week presets produce, which is what the §Screens block draws and what TC-03-E2E-12 reads off `calendar-range-label`.

REQ-03-015 — the reservation already exists: BUG-013 shipped `--range-col` on the `.time-off-calendar` block and `width: var(--range-col)` on `.time-off-calendar-range` (globals.css:877, :886-893). REQ-03-015 asks only that the reserved width cover the widest label **any** window can now produce, which the contracts file measures as `28 Dec 2026 – 14 Mar 2027`. Widen the existing property if that string does not fit at the shipped font, and update the comment above the block to name the four windows. **Do not add a second property for the same reservation** — the cases file calls it `--range-label-col`, but two custom properties reserving one width is the drift the DS-gap table exists to prevent; record the chosen name in the block comment.

REQ-03-014 / REQ-03-018 — the geometry. Add `--day-col-min` to the `.time-off-calendar` block and use it in both grid templates: `var(--name-col) repeat(N, minmax(var(--day-col-min), 1fr))` at CalendarScreen.tsx:75 (the skeleton) and :268 (the grid). Pick a value that keeps the two-line day header legible — around 32px — and note in the block comment that it must exceed roughly 11px or 92 columns still fit a 1280px viewport and TC-03-E2E-13's scroll assertion has nothing to observe.

REQ-03-018 — `.time-off-calendar-grid { min-width: max-content }` is today inside `@media (max-width: 1199px)` (globals.css:978-983). TC-03-E2E-13 reads the scroll at a 1280px viewport, above that breakpoint, so the rule must apply at every width. Make it unconditional and drop the media query; `.time-off-calendar-scroll` already carries `overflow-x: auto` (globals.css:965-967), so the container scrolls and the member column keeps its `position: sticky`.

Design system: import from `@devscribed/ds`, the package root only. No hardcoded colour or size in the TSX — the three new numbers are the custom properties above, declared in the one block that already declares `--name-col` and the band colours, with a reason beside each.

risks.risk: The empty selection resolves to `id: { in: [] }` and the route answers 200 with no rows — the failure mode that looks like success and that TC-03-INT-21 is the only thing standing in front of.
risks.mitigation: T2 names it explicitly; TC-03-INT-21 and TC-03-INT-22 both assert three members rather than merely a 200.

risks.risk: `packages/validation/dist` is stale after the two messages are deleted, so tsc and the static gate keep seeing them and the compile-time break this spec relies on never happens.
Widening `TimeOffCalendarWindow` to include 'range' forces `timeOffCalendarWindowRange` and `stepTimeOffCalendarAnchor` to invent a meaning for a window that has no anchor.
risks.mitigation: T1 adds `TimeOffCalendarWindowChoice` beside the preset union instead, and says why in the doc comment.

risks.risk: `--day-col-min` chosen too small: 92 columns then fit a 1280px viewport and TC-03-E2E-13's scroll assertion passes vacuously or fails confusingly.
risks.mitigation: T5 states the arithmetic — the floor must exceed roughly 11px at that viewport — and proposes ~32px, which is what the two-line day header needs anyway.

risks.risk: The Range window bypasses BUG-012's `isCurrentWindow` guard, and the grid draws the previous window while the header shows the new one.
risks.mitigation: T5 keeps the guard, which compares `data.range` against the range being displayed and therefore covers a custom range unchanged — but the implementer must confirm the custom range flows into the same `range` value the guard reads.

risks.risk: TC-03-E2E-13 measures a rendered box across four windows and three steps; a one-pixel difference from a font fallback fails it for a reason that is not the rule.
risks.mitigation: The reservation is a fixed width on the label, not a max-width, so the label's content cannot move its neighbours at all; assert equality of `x` on `calendar-today` only, as the case says.

risks.risk: Deleting the client-side short-circuit removes the only place the screen cleared `data` on an invalid scope; a scope change must still not leave the previous window's grid on screen.
risks.mitigation: `isCurrentWindow` already governs that, and the request is now always spent, so the skeleton draws while it is in flight.
